target: Feature parity is the requested target. No smaller V1 scope has been approved.

Node, mark, command, shortcut and decoration extensibility.
Table commands, selections and optional resizing.
Image presentation and optional inline/resize behavior; upload is a separate integration.
Yjs and IndexedDB offline integration; not Breditor's protocol.

StarterKit composition: Blockquote, Bold, Code, CodeBlock, Document, HardBreak, Heading, HorizontalRule, Italic, Link, Bullet/Ordered lists, ListItem, ListKeymap, Paragraph, Strike, Text, Underline, Dropcursor, Gapcursor, TrailingNode and UndoRedo.
Inspected command surface, table plugin wiring and separate HTML/Markdown converters.
Modern comparison target for the FCKeditor lineage; configurable UI and integrations.
More than 150 features/subfeatures, with premium labels. Rows below group related capabilities rather than copy that count.
Basic formatting baseline.
Rich table workflow, including capabilities beyond basic geometry.
External document paste is a dedicated feature, not internal clipboard equivalence.
Alternative data output pipeline.
Inspected separate input transformation, model insertion and output transformation stages. No source copied.
Open-source and commercial feature boundaries must be evaluated separately.

Source of the client-rendered Tiptap "Features" catalog: 96 entries in 23 groups with plan tags (tiptap-docs 013f78b, 2026-11-20; Tiptap v3.35.0).
Mention node with configurable suggestion triggers.

Show spaces, hard breaks and paragraph ends.

Paid Pages: page format, page-break node, headers/footers, footnotes, endnotes, zoom.
Paid DOCX import; the conversion family also exports DOCX, PDF, ODT, EPUB, DOC and Markdown.
Pilot Content Protection plus Slots and Variables (template fields).
Client and server AI Toolkit: schema-aware agent tools that read and edit the document.
Compare any two documents, client or server side.
List start, styles and reversed order (now premium).
Legal multi-level (1.1.1) numbering (premium).
Mentions with feeds and custom markers.
Slash commands (premium).
Inline bookmarks and internal links (now premium).
Page break (now premium).
Text part language (lang and dir).
Table captions.
Image linking.
Footnotes (premium, new).
Special characters picker (now premium).
Case change (premium).
Format painter (premium).
Automatic text transformations (autocorrect).
In-content table of contents widget (premium).
Show blocks; see also minimap.html and title.html.
Autosave plugin contract.
Menu bar; see also editor types and the accessibility help dialog.
Content Security Policy and Trusted Types; see also error-handling.html (watchdog).
CKEditor AI: chat, quick actions, review, translate, AI suggestions and MCP (premium).
Restricted editing (premium).

features.summary: Paragraph and heading editing
features.current: Rust rich actions and the shared editor support paragraphs, ranked headings, split/join and retained identity.
features.acceptance: Keep all six heading ranks, text formatting, local/shared history and recovery consistent in one installed V1 editor.

features.summary: Bold, italic, underline, strike and inline code
features.current: The explicit standard profile now has local/shared stock controls driven by Rust exact/mixed state, including marks, caret overrides, keyboard submission and one-group formatting history. Tests cover clipboard, exact reload, offline merge and selective Undo. Public distribution promotion and the remaining integrated V1 workflows are still open.
features.acceptance: Ship all everyday marks in the combined profile, renderer and toolbar; test mixed state, caret formats, clipboard, offline edits and selective Undo/Redo.

features.summary: Subscript and superscript
features.current: The experimental standard profile now has explicit script-switching controls in local/shared editors, with one Undo group and exact recovered history in cells/captions. The model still admits independent literals and never silently normalizes them. V1 promotion and complete foreign interchange remain open.
features.acceptance: Define mutually compatible script formats, semantic presentation and exact history/interchange behavior.

features.summary: Font family, size, text and background color
features.current: The standard profile now has local/shared mixed-value forms and reset controls for RGB24 text/background colors, integer 8..96 pixel sizes and four font-family presets. Empty resets preserve exact history and Redo. Arbitrary CSS/embedded fonts are unsupported; distribution promotion and foreign interchange remain open.
features.acceptance: Promote safe declarative presentations into the combined editor, define supported font/size/color domains and test interoperability.

features.summary: Links and automatic link detection
features.current: Default and explicit standard rich/shared Link forms reuse the same safe URL policy. Standard forms support mixed values, stale guards and exact history/reload. Explicit native property patches preserve each observed URL or target when the other form field is left blank; every selected character must already carry a Link. Complete set commands retain replacement semantics. Shared patches use original complete-format annotations and whole-format concurrent conflict policy, with atomic existing group limits. Foreign interchange, optional autolink and release qualification remain open. Opt-in autolink-v1 converts a typed http(s)/www URL on space or Enter into the standard link only when the target is already canonical under the native safeLinkV1 subset; trailing punctuation stays plain and one Undo removes only the link.
features.acceptance: Use one safe URL policy for shared rendering, explicit link editing, clipboard/export and optional autolink, without interpreting arbitrary HTML.

features.summary: Blockquotes, code blocks and horizontal rules
features.current: Explicit local/shared structural V2 provides quote, code and rule commands, safe rendering, code-language controls, same-block replacement and guarded code exit. Installed vanilla/React, reference relay, explicit/natural history and rich interchange paths exist; creator Undo retains peer text for later Redo/recovery. This is a functional candidate, not a frozen V1 grammar or completed physical-input, producer-fidelity and release qualification.
features.acceptance: Add original Rust contracts and separate actions for each kind, including code language/text rules, boundary navigation, shared conflict policy and migration.

features.summary: Hard breaks and navigation around atomic blocks
features.current:
Local/shared native hard breaks retain one LF, and logical navigation preserves atom stops, transparent containers, cell/caption domains, ranges, read-only policy and Redo. Separate commands create text beside atoms or delete/replace whole images, visible tables and rules. Rust chooses directional recovery and fresh floors for sole-child/hidden-only parent remainders; plain/first-key replacement retains exact original-family history and peer causal text. V2 routes reach installed vanilla/React, including natural first-key history and reload. Missing first-key beforeinput and uncancelled paging defaults have reproduced controller repairs. Shared replacement needs transient insertion headroom. Physical/bidi arrows, gap/drop positions, general ranges, already hidden-only documents, native OS atom clipboard/input and final reliability qualification remain incomplete. Typing after a line break at the very end of a text block now lands after it in Chromium and WebKit: the live renderer adds a presentation-only trailing
anchor (no content or offset change).
features.acceptance: Specify soft-break semantics, create reachable text positions around every atom, and test Shift+Enter, arrows, deletion and empty-document recovery.

features.summary: Bullet and numbered nested lists
features.current: Rich and shared paths implement indentation, outdentation, item split/join and list conversion with retained content.
features.acceptance: Retain the same list contract in the V1 installable profile and native/browser mixed-content tests.

features.summary: Interactive task lists
features.current: Explicit local/shared structural V2 provides typed completion, pointer/Space checkboxes, item split/join, nesting, conversion and empty exit. General and document selections, Rust-admitted rich clipboard and the optional foreign adapter now reach the installed mixed workflow. Offline completion versus nesting, selective history and exact recovery are covered by focused native/SDK/relay tests. Public V1 promotion, broader producer fidelity and physical-input/reliability qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Add typed checked state with keyboard and pointer behavior, nesting, clipboard, conflict policy and author-local history.

features.summary: List numbering and marker properties
features.current: Positive ordered-list starts are supported. Rich language V4 (released, frozen) adds five ordered numbering styles (decimal, lower/upper alpha, lower/upper roman) and HTML-compatible reversed counting, as one history group, locally and in shared V4 (`set_list_numbering`, with a start change in the same Undo group; a split list's tail keeps its style and counting order), with local and shared toolbar controls and identical HTML/Markdown/DOCX interchange and Office paste in local and shared V4 editors. An opt-in presentation-only legal multi-level numbering mode (`legalListNumbering`) derives 1.1.1 markers from admitted starts and reversal (docs/LIST_STRUCTURE.md). This covers Tiptap's OrderedList start/type. Missing: bullet marker styles, decimal-leading-zero and other counter styles, stored legal multi-level numbering (needs a new language version) and per-item overrides.
features.acceptance: Define each numbering/style domain, restart/continuation behavior and deterministic nested export, cover bullet styles and legal multi-level numbering or record them as approved exclusions, and release V4, before claiming advanced list parity.

features.summary: Alignment, block indent, direction and line height controls
features.current: Explicit layout V3 provides bounded native alignment, indent, direction and line-height fields, independent shared updates, safe rendering and mixed/inherited vanilla/React controls. The optional interchange adapter carries representable layout with explicit HTML fallback/loss notices. Installed mixed editing and focused offline/recovery matrices exercise this candidate; complete bidi editing, broader producer fidelity and V1 qualification remain unfinished.
features.acceptance: Add bounded semantic block properties, direction-aware selection/layout and safe rendering/interchange, not arbitrary stored CSS.

features.summary: Text, node, grid and document-wide editing selections
features.current: Explicit general and document scopes now cover partial table/image preservation, rich Copy with empty unselected cells, atomic deletion/replacement, Enter/composition and whole-document Select All without manufacturing text endpoints. Caption/code flow/grid paste uses the approved text-with-loss notice policy. Installed mixed workflows combine both history policies, foreign paste, offline authors, fresh IDs, exact recovery and peer-preserving Undo/Redo through writer transport V2. Original defaults and saved families remain distinct. Physical input, supported-environment reliability, public API/migration and final V1 qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Specify and implement document-wide Select All, deletion, replacement and formatting across lists, tables, captions and atoms in both directions.

features.summary: Undo, Redo and natural typing groups
features.current: Exact local/selective shared history and compound formatting are implemented. Native local and shared typing now reach opt-in Wasm, vanilla/React, durable sessions and DOM boundaries in both languages. Separate declared families preserve exact grouped recovery; original defaults/models/frames stay unchanged and older runtimes reject requested unsupported modes. Atomic legacy upgrades retain Redo, failed saves retain recovery, and invisible Undo publications autosave. The relay's original-only identity check was reproduced and repaired without weakening writer/model checks. Final installed matrices pass 288 SDK and 78 application cases, including format/move/composition/async/offline/online/restart history. Private bounded projection caches preserve independent fresh replay and atomic rejection; final diagnostics do not establish a reliable Firefox speedup. History remains partial: recorded Firefox method calls take multiple seconds after a mixed editing sequence and can exceed the unchanged 750ms group gap. Historical WebKit startup recurred in an intermediate run; older replay/cancel observations and an unclassified offline-button observation remain open. The shared replay journal also remains bounded at 1,000 entries and 16 MiB; this is not a rolling 1,000-action Undo window. Client/relay lifecycle rotation and retained-version/asset policy are unresolved V1 storage work. Slash commands now run as one native replaceTriggerThen history group (trigger removal plus one allowlisted block command, atomic, exact Undo/Redo and checkpoint restore), and shared slash batches are proven to undo as one group.
features.acceptance: Define typing/paste/composition/format/move grouping, preserve remote work under local Undo, and test future Redo after recovery.

features.summary: Breditor structural clipboard
features.current: The original rich clipboard now also reaches general/document selections, preserving partially selected structures and empty unselected table cells. Guarded Copy/Cut/Paste uses Rust admission with fresh identities, one history group and exact recovery in local/shared owners. Optional foreign formats are supplied by the separate interchange adapter; native clipboard and final release qualification remain distinct.
features.acceptance: Keep exact source preservation, one-step cut/paste history and cross-peer clipboard behavior in the installed V1 editor.

features.summary: Sanitized HTML import and semantic export
features.current: The opt-in @breditor/interchange adapter imports inert bounded HTML and emits allowlisted semantic HTML through Rust clipboard admission. Local/shared managed and React openings provide explicit priority, stale guards, four-format retention, host-owned image mapping and post-publication loss notices. Clean-installed round trips and mixed editing/recovery workflows pass. Arbitrary HTML/CSS, captured-producer fidelity and physical clipboard/final release qualification remain outside that claim.
features.acceptance: Build separate import/export adapters with declared loss diagnostics, resource bounds, URL policy, asset references and rich round-trip fixtures.

features.summary: Markdown import, export and paste
features.current: The separate optional adapter implements a named version-one CommonMark-based dialect with tables, strikethrough, task markers and sanitized raw HTML. It imports/exports through native schema validation and advertises Markdown MIME explicitly; ordinary text is never guessed as Markdown. Safe HTML fallback and compatibility/loss notices cover unrepresentable layout, rich tables, captions and exact code. This is not full GFM conformance or completed release qualification. Export now alternates list markers so adjacent lists stay separate, emits hard breaks, GFM column alignment, empty fences and safe images as Markdown, and reports dropped fence info and raw HTML comments as losses; ordered starts below 1 become 1 with a list-numbering notice. Markdown import optionally links GFM autolink literals (autolinks: true) under the same candidate grammar and canonical link subset as typed autolink-v1.
features.acceptance: Choose a versioned Markdown subset, preserve representable semantics, report losses for merges/styles/media and test round trips.

features.summary: Word, Google Docs and spreadsheet rich paste
features.current: Representative Word/Docs/Excel markup fixtures exercise bounded stylesheet/list/table/merge conversion, formatting, links and host-owned images through the same Rust admission and paste actions. Combined installed offline/history/restart workflows cover those fixtures and explicit destination losses. They are authored representative snippets, not captured application-native clipboard certification; real producer fixtures and broader fidelity remain required. A reconstructed producer corpus (Word desktop/web, Google Docs/Sheets, Excel, LibreOffice, Cocoa), explicitly not captured certification, now drives exact structure/loss tests; nested Docs/Cocoa lists, Word lettered/roman/skipped levels, Word web list rebuilding, Docs script marks and file: image losses are handled. Real captured dumps remain required. Word desktop and Word for the web lettered/roman list numbering now maps to V4 list styles for owners that support list numbering.
features.acceptance: Maintain real producer fixtures and sanitization/loss policies; test lists, styles, tables, links and images through the same Rust admission boundary.

features.summary: Table geometry, cell bodies and grid operations
features.current: Creation/removal, row/column edits/moves, headers, merge/split, width values, rich cells and grid navigation/clipboard are functionally tested.
features.acceptance: Preserve the complete command set, rich content and selective history under the production package and all supported engines.

features.summary: Table presentation and advanced interaction
features.current: Width and header controls exist, plus opt-in accessible column-resize separators (one width command per drag or key, clamped to 32..4096). Rich language V4 adds an optional trailing table caption with add/remove commands and table-action, navigation, clipboard, search and HTML interchange, locally and in shared V4 (`add_table_caption`/`remove_table_caption`, one Undo step; a second concurrent caption stays hidden), with identical `<caption>` import and export in shared V4. Missing: table and cell styling (borders, backgrounds, padding, cell alignment), caption placement choice, table scrolling and layout tables. Nested tables are intentionally rejected.
features.acceptance: Resolve nested-table policy explicitly; add captions, accessible resize handles, table/cell presentation and interoperable rich paste without losing source partitions.

features.summary: Block raster images and durable assets
features.current: PNG/JPEG/WebP admission, paste/drop, alt/decorative, captions, dimensions, replacement/removal, offline uploads and cross-host bytes are implemented. Explicit whole-store raster archives now retain exact bytes, queue states and cancellation epochs, with canonical framing and atomic empty-destination restore. They are not automatically coordinated with native sessions, outboxes or server state.
features.acceptance: Preserve byte-first durability, binding epochs, cancelled uploads and independent document/asset save indicators in the V1 package.

features.summary: Image layouts, handles, links and external sources
features.current: Numeric dimensions and block captions work. Opt-in accessible resize handles (aspect-keeping corner, edges, keyboard, RTL-aware) exist for local and shared editors. Rich language V4 adds image links (canonical http(s) targets, optional new window, inert while editing), locally and in shared V4 (`set_image_link` as one paired field, refused on decorative images), importing and exporting identically in both. Missing: inline and wrapped image styles, responsive variants, insert-by-URL with a safe remote-ingestion policy.
features.acceptance: Define supported layouts and ingestion policy, then test resize gestures, responsive output, link/alt behavior and asset lifecycle. Do not turn remote URLs into implicit server fetches.

features.summary: Simultaneous rich editing and selective history
features.current: Rust replicas and the reference relay integrate concurrent text, list, table and image edits while retaining author-local Undo/Redo.
features.acceptance: Keep the native contracts and independent-browser mixed workflow passing against the final released artifacts.

features.summary: Offline editing, reconnect and exact reload
features.current: Exclusive writer ownership, durable local journals, queued uploads, reconnect and exact reload work through browser and network tests. Independently verified archives preserve document, review and raster data through non-overwriting recovery. Native server-log and independent document and comment history generations preserve offline work and future Undo/Redo. Source and independently installed activation-intent suites exercise authenticated whole-room restart and publication, retained metadata and fourteen offline lanes, asset state and provider reconciliation. The relay process recovery tests verify acknowledged edits, comments and an upload after exit before a new snapshot. Portable predecessor compaction retires raw archives and redundant checkpoints from all three checkpoint versions while preserving the selected terminal cut, offline work and Undo/Redo. Supported lifetime limits and final durability qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Qualify supported history/document limits and operational recovery, not only the normal offline/reconnect path.

features.summary: Authenticated peer carets and selections
features.current: Lease-bound ephemeral presence resolves causal text/node/grid anchors and paints a separate read-only overlay.
features.acceptance: Retain expiry, fencing and read-only behavior; qualify overlay placement and accessibility in the supported layouts.

features.summary: Permissions and application authentication
features.current: Reference-room Reader/Editor authority and revocation are enforced. Explicit native routers can additionally use a separate durable serving epoch with real process-level locks; every native transaction and private capture rechecks it. The current Unix reference backend requires one protected non-rollback authority namespace and does not complete client/provider reconciliation or authenticated recovery activation. The local demo bootstrap is not public login, tenant provisioning or TLS deployment.
features.acceptance: Provide host identity adapters, room lifecycle, secure credential storage, observable denial/revocation and deployment guidance with independent authorization tests.

features.summary: Native live read-only editing
features.current: Both rich languages have native local/shared host policy, initial SDK options and live vanilla/React setters. It rejects authoring, pending styles and history while retaining selection, copy, incoming updates and durability. Surface/captions, task widgets, toolbar, keyboard, beforeinput, Cut-as-Copy, composition queues and asynchronous assets share the policy. Lock/unlock fences old intents without a history entry. Policy is not stored permission: restored owners start editable and hosts reapply it. Installed three-engine and real-relay tests pass; editable-region restrictions are tracked separately.
features.acceptance: Enforce read-only consistently for keyboard, beforeinput, clipboard, API, toolbar, composition and remote updates; define editable-region restrictions separately.

features.summary: Editable region restrictions
features.current: Native block-region restricted editing (docs/RESTRICTED_EDITING.md): a live host policy outside the frozen V4 grammar names editable subtrees by retained block ids. Rust admits every local command, mixed request, pending style and Undo/Redo by its complete effect, and anything that would change protected content is refused whole (`breditor_rich.restricted`). Cross-region selections are refused, not clamped; leaf regions refuse Enter and boundary merges while container regions allow new blocks; Undo of protected history is refused. Local Wasm, DOM and SDK provide `restrictedEditing:{policy}`, Tab/Shift+Tab region navigation, presentation-only region marking and Rust-derived toolbar disabling, qualified in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Shared owners enforce the same rule natively for local work while incoming peer changes stay unfiltered; the policy is a host input, never persisted. Missing: inline exceptions (a V5 delta), shared DOM/SDK wiring and relay or server enforcement.
features.acceptance: Define and enforce protected/editable identities through cross-region selections, moves, atomic mixed requests, pending styles, history authorization and remote changes; qualify persistence and host/server authority separately.

features.summary: Composable feature and custom-node SDK
features.current: Typed inline declarations, profile fingerprints and custom toolbar callbacks exist. Shared structural grammar is sealed; arbitrary custom blocks/node views are not a supported extension SDK. The typed inline seam now carries a first-party extension end to end (ruby: manifest, own fingerprint, generic commands and history, shared merging, closed presentation, interchange and toolbar controls).
features.acceptance: Stabilize Breditor-owned schema/action/render/converter capabilities, dependencies, failure isolation and conformance tests without adopting another editor's protocol.

features.summary: Expandable toolbars, context menus and selection UI
features.current: Local/shared standard controls now share field widgets and Rust-derived state, keyboard actions, editor focus return and stale-draft rejection. Owner-bound controls reject another editor before host mutation; custom owner-neutral controls remain reusable. Default compiled action-state APIs remain distinct. Opt-in floating selection toolbars and keyboard-reachable context menus now borrow admitted controls through the same widget, Rust-derived state, gating, command path and focus return for local and shared editors; the same borrowed-control contract drives an opt-in menu bar, empty-line block menu and balloon-block preset (editor-shell-and-help), and these surfaces are covered in real browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) for focus, keyboard and shared Rust-derived state. Screen-reader qualification is open.
features.acceptance: One command/state contract must drive buttons, keyboard, forms and context menus with active/mixed/disabled state and consistent focus return.

features.summary: Find and replace
features.current: The optional Rust rich core has source-bound Unicode literal/regex search, semantic table/caption traversal and atomic local/shared Replace One/All. Opaque Wasm/SDK results, borrowed vanilla/React controls, separate shared/document startup and search-aware persistence retain exact history, failed saves and writer leases. Independent installed mixed table/caption, comment/version and offline-peer workflows pass; a headless Chromium production example checks actual highlight geometry, readonly navigation and one-step Undo. Shared splices preserve original-character provenance. The feature remains a candidate: old save keys are not auto-migrated, managed document-only startup does not persist review metadata, and API/performance/platform/release promotion remains open.
features.acceptance: Define literal/Unicode search, navigation and replace-all as one bounded semantic action, excluding hidden or noneditable content by explicit policy.

features.summary: Markdown shortcuts and automatic text transformations
features.current: An explicit Rust policy plans bounded heading/list/quote/task/code/rule and simple inline shortcuts using existing semantic actions and exact history families. Exclusive plain/natural calls retain literal input and isolate conversion Undo. Immutable markdown-v1 opt-in is connected through native-capability-checked vanilla/root/React owners, source-bound callback cancellation, ordinary composition/paste/range/remote exclusions and accepted-input refusal reporting. Independent installed consumers exercise public types, exact reopen and bundle isolation. Existing-list task conversion, adjacent/nested automatic behavior, conventional code Enter and final qualification remain unfinished. A repaired whole-source replacement endpoint requires the fixed shared reader; affected older readers reject that newly supported case. markdown-v1 now also converts an existing bullet item to a task ([ ] / [x]), joins a marker typed right after a matching list into that list, and exits a code block on three trailing Enters, each as one isolated Undo step, locally and in shared editors. Rule sets now include opt-in `typography-v1` (automatic text transformations) alongside `markdown-v1` and `autolink-v1`.
features.acceptance: Add deterministic opt-in rules with composition exclusion, remote-edit boundaries and one-step Undo behavior.

features.summary: Mentions and slash commands
features.current: V4 mention entities (closed kinds user/page/tag, identity = kind + id, label snapshot, `@` marker only) are atomic and inserted by one guarded command in one Undo step, locally and in shared V4 (`insert_mention`, shared `@` menu `mountSharedMentions` / SDK `mountMentions`, atomicity repair under concurrency). Slash commands are one native Undo group locally (`replaceTriggerThen`) and one guarded shared batch, with V4 items for collapsible sections and page breaks. Mention spans import and export identically in local and shared V4 editors. Open: several trigger characters and host-declared kinds or prefixes (`#`) and mention output customization.
features.acceptance: Specify entity identity, async suggestion cancellation, accessible menus and command execution through Rust rather than DOM mutation.

features.summary: Counts, placeholder, fullscreen and outline
features.current: Native Rust counts and a stable-ID outline derive accepted body text; optional Wasm/SDK reads and borrowed vanilla/React controls retain exact save/history families. Native placeholder eligibility keeps literal hints outside durable/editable/clipboard content, with admitted startup and live labels. A separately owned browser fullscreen controller borrows the existing local/shared/document coordinator, preserves exact publications and logical selections, keeps remote edits flowing, and never adopts/exits a foreign session. Replaceable vanilla/React controls do not close the controller or writer; native cleanup is asynchronous and retryable. Current/pinned-reader workflows, isolated installs and focused headless Chromium production checks exercise these candidates. Physical Escape/input, cross-platform, performance and final V1 qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Derive counts/outline from admitted AST snapshots, keep placeholders out of content, and preserve focus/selection through fullscreen transitions.

features.summary: Block rearrangement and drop feedback
features.current: File drop and typed block/axis moves exist. Local and shared editors have an opt-in block drag handle with a semantic drop resolver, drop cursor, keyboard pick-up/move and Alt+Shift+Arrow steps, each sending one retained-ID move (shared `move_block` at the planned revision; local native MoveBlock in one exact history group). Missing: inline content drag between positions and a general drop cursor for content drags.
features.acceptance: Move retained IDs rather than copy/delete; add keyboard equivalents and test invalid/cyclic/cross-container targets and shared Undo.

features.summary: Media, details, emoji, math and diagrams
features.current: Rich language V4 adds an original collapsible section (breditor/details with one text-only summary and a flow body, nesting bounded at 8, persisted open state) with wrap/unwrap/open-state commands, deterministic editing, live/static rendering and HTML/Markdown interchange, locally and in shared V4 (`wrap_details`, `unwrap_details`, `set_details_open`, toolbar and slash items, one Undo step each). Shared Enter at a collapsed summary expands it and enters the body in one guarded step like local `enterDetailsBody`, and `<details>` interchange is identical in shared V4. Emoji, mathematics (Tiptap now ships KaTeX math open source), media embeds, audio/video, iframes and diagrams remain missing.
features.acceptance: Use separate original node contracts, inert/sandboxed renderers and explicit providers. Define import/export and collaboration for each admitted widget.

features.summary: Framework integrations and static rendering
features.current: The private SDK supplies installed local and durable shared vanilla/React entry points. Shared replacement waits for exact old-writer closure; failed save or startup cleanup hands off journal recovery without implicit discard. Tests cover StrictMode, cancellation, rerenders, actual reload, quota failures and database upgrade retention in all three engines. Local-only and shared-without-React installs remain independent. SSR is a starting placeholder, not a static document renderer. Public API/package decisions, remaining source promotion and broader framework/static-renderer examples remain open. An inert DOM-free static renderer (@breditor/editor/static) and React BreditorStaticDocument now render validated documents with the live link policy, table merge resolution and block layout; docs cover Vue/Svelte/Angular adapter responsibility.
features.acceptance: Ship installed-package React and vanilla examples, stable lifecycle hooks and an inert data renderer; document adapter responsibility for other frameworks.

features.summary: Threaded comments and review annotations
features.current: Opt-in native/Wasm/SDK and vanilla/React controls provide durable attributed discussions, mapped/orphaned anchors, resolution, independent comment history, authenticated comment authority and offline transport/recovery. Clean-installed combined review/asset workflows exercise exact reopens and host restart. Host identity/tenant integration and final platform/storage qualification remain release gates, not comments API claims.
features.acceptance: Design durable mapped anchors, thread permissions, resolution/orphan policy, offline merging and independent comment history before building UI.

features.summary: Suggestions and tracked changes
features.current: Source-bound attributed text, formatting, list, table and image proposals leave accepted content unchanged until an authenticated once-only server decision. Offline decision queues, owned accepted-effect Undo/Redo, manual revisions and bounded automatic formatting/text rebasing reach installed vanilla/React controls. Accepted document export remains separate from proposal/review metadata and outboxes. Explicit review-aware export qualification, production permissions and release promotion remain open; mixed-command automatic text rebase is unsupported.
features.acceptance: Define suggestions for text, formatting, lists, tables and images with attribution, permissions, concurrent accept/reject and explicit export semantics.

features.summary: Named versions, comparison and restore
features.current: Immutable named versions retain source proofs, semantic comparison and explicit guarded restore as a fresh edit. An authenticated shared catalog, optional SDK cache and borrowed vanilla/React controls preserve independent document/review journals and fresh writer identity. Clean-installed combined workflows cover stale/conflicting restore, exact recovery, offline edits and host restart. Asset retention, bounded catalog/journal lifetime and final production qualification remain open release gates.
features.acceptance: Separate user-facing document versions from runtime journals and GC; restore without reusing old writer identity or overwriting concurrent work.

features.summary: Word, PDF and other office document conversion
features.current: A dependency-free deterministic DOCX exporter (@breditor/interchange/docx, STORE-only zip, fixed timestamps) maps headings, inline formats, links, lists incl. V4 numbering, quotes, code, rules, page breaks, tables with merges and captions, host-supplied images and bookmarks, reporting every unrepresentable feature as a loss. DOCX import, PDF/ODT and opening in Word/LibreOffice are not qualified.
features.acceptance: Choose self-hostable adapters, licensing and fidelity targets; preserve document/asset bindings and report unsupported content instead of silently dropping it.

features.summary: Pages, page breaks and print layout
features.current: Breditor stays a flow editor (docs/PAGINATION_AND_PRINT.md). Rich language V4 adds an explicit root-level page-break block (insert/delete, node selection, navigation stop, clipboard, Word/Docs/CSS page-break import), locally and in shared V4 (`insert_page_break`/`delete_page_break`, slash item, rendered separator), plus an opt-in CSS print layer (A4/Letter, orientation, margins, break avoidance, repeated header rows, approximate preview guides). No measured pagination, page numbers, running headers/footers, footnotes/endnotes or zoom (Tiptap Pages, CKEditor Pagination) Word, Google Docs and CSS page breaks import identically in local and shared V4 editors.
features.acceptance: Qualify print output in real browsers and either specify measured pagination with page numbers and running headers or record the flow-editor decision as an approved exclusion.

features.summary: Templates, merge fields, footnotes and bookmarks
features.current: Rich language V4 adds unique named bookmarks on text blocks and `#name` internal links, locally and in shared V4 (`set_bookmark`, `rename_bookmark` retargeting every link in one group, document-order uniqueness repair, bookmark index): dangling links are allowed but reported, and HTML anchors, Markdown fallback and DOCX bookmarks interchange identically in local and shared V4. Bookmarks attach to blocks, not arbitrary inline positions (CKEditor places inline anchors), and cut drops them. Footnotes/endnotes, templates, merge fields, template slots/variables and cross-reference fields are missing.
features.acceptance: Design reference integrity, field/value trust, permissions and shared history; define behavior when referenced content is moved or removed.

features.summary: AI assistance and integrated spelling or grammar review
features.current: An opt-in provider-agnostic contract exists for local and shared editors: hosts supply rewrite and language-check providers, only explicitly scoped plain text is sent with cancellation, deadlines and size bounds, provider output is validated as untrusted, rewrites are reviewed and applied as one guarded command with stale refusal (in shared editors, one guarded native plain-text range replacement that stales only when its target region changes), and language issues are painted outside the editing DOM. An opt-in agent tool contract adds schema-validated, revision-bound, reviewable agent edits (see ai-agents-and-server-api). Missing: formatted-scope requests, bundled providers, AI chat and translation UI (host concerns, as with Tiptap and CKEditor) and autocomplete.
features.acceptance: Define explicit host providers and privacy boundaries; generated edits must use ordinary guarded commands with stale-result rejection and reviewable history.

features.summary: Source editing, general HTML and email layouts
features.current: Canonical schema-bound AST editing deliberately does not preserve arbitrary HTML/CSS, full-page metadata or email layout markup. The scope is now explicit: page metadata, email layout, scripts and stored CSS are out of scope. An opt-in document-selection source view edits sanitized semantic HTML in a textarea, previews bounded allowlist losses before any change and applies one guarded whole-document paste; shared and ordinary families have no source view.
features.acceptance: Resolve the compatibility scope explicitly. Any source UI must import through a bounded allowlist and loss report; never store executable HTML as trusted editor state.

features.summary: Multiple editable roots in one document
features.current: Local rich editors support multiple editable roots as a root set of ordinary V1–V4 documents with no grammar change (docs/MULTIPLE_ROOTS.md): stable root ids, labels, attributes and order; one active root (cross-root selections are not expressible by design, as in CKEditor); and one native history owner that keeps a single global Undo/Redo order across roots and routes Undo/Redo to the owning root. `mountRichMultiRootEditor` mounts one surface per root with one shared toolbar that follows focus, with per-root data, add/remove root and a versioned `breditor/rich-root-set` checkpoint that re-verifies every root's history. Missing: undoable add/remove root and root attributes, shared real-time multi-root (specified: one room per root, a client journal and a replicated set manifest) and whole-set interchange.
features.acceptance: Specify root identity, cross-root selections, shared ordering and one history owner before advertising multi-root parity.

features.summary: Localized UI, bidirectional content and language metadata
features.current: Unicode text is retained. An opt-in validated UI catalog localizes local and shared chrome, toolbars, context UI, slash, resize and drag handles, the search, writing, fullscreen, review and suggestion panels, clipboard status lines and code-keyed user refusals, with chrome-only lang/dir; default English output is byte-identical and only English ships. Rich language V4 adds canonical BCP 47 text-run language (`lang`), locally and in shared V4 (`setTextLanguage`, Language control), with identical `lang`/`xml:lang` interchange. Missing: inline `dir` on language runs (direction stays independent by design), shipped translations, localized native error strings and qualified mixed-direction (RTL/bidi) editing.
features.acceptance: Separate UI language from content direction, localize control strings and qualify mixed-direction navigation/selection with language metadata.

features.summary: Skip-level lists, multi-block list items and legal multi-level numbering
features.current: Rich V1–V4 already admit multi-block list items (a leading paragraph or heading followed by any flow, including paragraphs after a child list). Native JoinListItems/SplitListItem block captures (exact inverses, one Undo step each) back local `joinListItems` `blocks` / `splitListItemBlock` and shared `join_list_items` `blocks` / `split_list_item_block`, with CKEditor-style keys in local and shared editors: Backspace in an empty item head keeps it as a later block of the previous item, Enter in an empty later block splits it out, and Tab/Shift+Tab indent and outdent from any block. HTML, Markdown and DOCX handling of multi-block items is tested. Legal multi-level numbering is an opt-in, presentation-only `legalListNumbering` option. Missing: skip-level items and stored legal numbering, both needing a grammar change (specified as a V5 candidate in docs/LIST_STRUCTURE.md), task-item multi-block keys, and keyboard/screen-reader qualification.
features.acceptance: Specify multi-block items, skip-level structure and legal counters through native list actions, history, shared replay and interchange, or record each as an approved exclusion.

features.summary: Syntax-highlighted code blocks
features.current: An opt-in local and shared SDK decorator derives bounded CSS highlight ranges from explicit JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, Python and Rust labels. Static HTML can use the same tokenizer and palette to publish escaped syntax-colored code. Editor DOM, selection offsets and serialized content are unchanged. Unsupported languages display plain code.
features.acceptance: Qualify the bounded language set and styling on the supported browser matrix and exact release candidate. Record supported languages and plain-code fallback in integration docs.

features.summary: Typographic replacements and autocorrect
features.current: Opt-in native `typography-v1` input-rule set (`inputRules: "typography-v1"` or `{rule, include, exclude, quotes}`): smart quotes with apostrophes and locale presets (English, German, French with no-break spaces, Swiss, Polish) or a validated custom pair; ellipsis, delimited en/em dashes, (c)/(r)/(tm), delimited fractions and arrows, <=/>=/!= and an opt-in misc group. Rules are chosen by CKEditor-style groups and names, validated natively and at mount. Each replacement is one native Undo group that restores exactly the typed characters and keeps their formats; nothing converts in code, on paste, during IME composition, on remote updates or when read-only. Local and shared editors behave identically. Not supported: CKEditor `extra` custom rules, Tiptap per-rule output overrides and RTL swap, and undelimited `--`, `->` and `2x3` forms.
features.acceptance: Add opt-in, locale-aware replacements as native input rules with one-step Undo of the replacement, composition safety and shared parity.

features.summary: Special characters, case change, format painter and named styles
features.current: Opt-in special characters, case change and format painter for local and shared rich editors (docs/FORMATTING_PRODUCTIVITY.md). The picker has five built-in categories, validated host categories, name and code-point search, an accessible keyboard grid and localized names, inserting through native text input in one Undo step. Case change is a native Rust command (local `changeSelectionCase`, shared guarded `ReplaceTextRange` splices): UPPER, lower, Title Case with configurable minor words and Shift+F3 cycling, full Unicode mapping (ß→SS, final sigma, titlecase digraphs; Turkic i only for an explicit tr/az locale), preserving format runs, identities and mentions in one Undo step that converges across peers. The format painter copies inline text formatting (single-use, double-click sticky, Escape cancels) and applies it as one selection-format change. Named styles and highlight presets are an intentional difference: inline formats are a fixed typed set and hosts compose presets from typed format commands.
features.acceptance: Specify each tool through existing typed format commands (one Undo step, local and shared) or record named styles as an approved difference.

features.summary: In-document table of contents
features.current: The local and shared editor contents presentation nests native heading reads and navigates with revision-guarded selection. Static HTML can prepend a linked contents list using stable heading IDs and existing bookmark anchors. Placement is host-controlled.
features.acceptance: Define or explicitly scope the movable, saved contents block, scroll tracking and non-HTML export behavior. Qualify the selected workflow on exact release artifacts.

features.summary: Show blocks, invisible characters, minimap, document title and focus styling
features.current: Opt-in show-blocks, invisible-character and focused-block aids (`mountRichEditingAids`; SDK `mountEditingAids`) work in local and shared editors (docs/EDITING_AIDS.md). Show blocks outlines every rendered block and labels its type from the UI catalog; invisible characters marks spaces, no-break spaces, tabs, hard breaks and paragraph ends; an optional attribute follows the caret's block. Everything is painted in an aria-hidden, pointer-transparent layer outside the editable DOM, and toggling (buttons or Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift+B/P) is never a command, publication or Undo step and leaves caret movement, typing, Copy and static output unchanged, checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Missing: a content minimap and a separate document-title field (a title would be document structure the frozen V4 grammar does not have).
features.acceptance: Add each aid as an inert presentation layer that never enters the document model, with accessibility checks.

features.summary: Ruby (furigana) annotations
features.current: Ruby is an opt-in first-party typed inline extension, `breditor-ruby/ruby`, with one required 1–256 byte annotation and no grammar change; profiles that include it get their own fingerprint while V1–V4 stay frozen (docs/RUBY_ANNOTATIONS.md). Local and shared Ruby and Remove ruby controls set, replace or remove a validated reading on a selection or the caret's group, each as one Undo step through the generic typed-format commands, with exact replay and shared convergence; typing never inherits a reading. Live and static output render `<ruby>base<rp>(</rp><rt>…</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>` with the live reading as non-editable generated content. HTML import/export maps `<ruby>` for ruby-capable local and shared owners, Markdown falls back to exact HTML and DOCX writes `w:ruby`. Not supported: nested or double-sided ruby and position options.
features.acceptance: Specify ruby as a typed inline structure with base/annotation text, selection, history, rendering and interchange, or record an approved exclusion.

features.summary: Autosave contract for rich and shared sessions
features.current: Base-text sessions have a checkpoint autosave; shared sessions persist durably; the rich local SDK has no implicit autosave (hosts save explicitly).
features.acceptance: Specify a debounced, ordered, failure-reporting autosave for rich local sessions (or document explicit saving as the contract) and qualify it with reload and failure tests.

features.summary: Menu bar, editor layouts and keyboard help dialog
features.current: Opt-in editor shell for local, shared and SDK rich editors (docs/EDITOR_SHELL.md): a WAI-ARIA menu bar (Alt+F9, arrows, typeahead, Escape back to the text; configurable menus checked at mount) and an empty-line block menu (Alt+F10; never takes focus) borrow admitted toolbar controls, so items show the same Rust-derived state and run one command and one Undo step (one guarded dispatch when shared). An Alt+0 modal help dialog (focus trap, platform-aware keys, localized) lists a read-only shortcut registry built from the editors' own chords and mounted add-ons, and a balloon-block preset composes the selection toolbar, block menu and help. Covered by jsdom contracts, rich-browser specs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit and a two-writer shared spec. Missing: real screen-reader qualification.
features.acceptance: Add a menu bar and shortcut help dialog built from admitted controls and the shortcut registry, with keyboard and screen-reader qualification.

features.summary: AI agents, document server API and webhooks
features.current: An opt-in, provider-agnostic agent tool contract (docs/AI_AGENT_TOOLS.md) gives a host's LLM nine typed tools with closed JSON Schemas to read the document in chunks, find text, read the selection and edit by block id and offset. Every call is validated as untrusted input against the schema, the document and the native grammar, bounded, bound to the revision the agent read and re-based only when every target is unchanged. Edits are reviewable by default: a staged change set accepted as one native publication and Undo step (native `commandGroup` locally, one guarded shared dispatch in rooms) or suggestion proposals; direct mode is opt-in; a review panel and an MCP-shaped adapter are included with no bundled model or network code. The reference relay adds an opt-in authenticated document server (docs/DOCUMENT_SERVER_API.md): room listing, canonical JSON snapshots with an exact revision, room creation, owner-only archive, comment threads, server-side injection of allowlisted native shared commands at an exact base revision as a service writer (one history group that clients see as a normal remote change), and HMAC-signed webhooks with retries and a delivery log. Missing: AI chat and translate UI (host concerns), relay-backed agent proposals, identity-provider auth, version and bulk endpoints, Rust HTML/Markdown export, durable webhook queues and outbound TLS (public-relay gate).
features.acceptance: Define a bounded, authenticated tool and server API over the native core (read, propose as suggestions, apply) with audit and authority checks before claiming parity.

features.summary: Content Security Policy guidance and crash restart
features.current: Journal recovery and exact reload exist; there is no documented CSP/Trusted Types policy for the Wasm runtime and no watchdog that restarts a crashed editor.
features.acceptance: Document and test a strict CSP (including Wasm requirements) and an opt-in crash-restart path that restores from durable state.

gates.acceptance: Expand grouped rows into versioned acceptance cases for every selected Tiptap/CKEditor capability. Group counts are not a parity percentage; record intentional differences and obtain approval for exclusions. The 2026-11-21 review mapped the current catalogs (Tiptap 3.35, 96 catalog entries; CKEditor 5 v49.1) to rows, added rows for uncovered capabilities and listed exclusions awaiting approval in docs/V1_RELEASE_PLAN.md; per-capability acceptance cases are still to be written.

gates.summary: Promote rich/shared Rust, Wasm and browser packages
gates.acceptance: Independent clean consumers install one supported paired profile and production module; no experiments path, manual target artifact or source-only link is required.

gates.summary: Freeze V1 APIs and explicit migration contracts
gates.acceptance: Document source, ABI, schema, journal and asset compatibility separately; add supported old-version recovery/migration fixtures and deliberate rejection paths.

gates.summary: Cover every distributed feature in the release pipeline
gates.acceptance: Default verify:release alone is insufficient. Run default, rich, shared, relay and installed-consumer checks reproducibly in CI, retaining exact candidate hashes and failed runs.

gates.summary: Qualify browser faults and native clipboard
gates.acceptance: Close or explicitly resolve the historical WebKit fault with a reproducible cause/fix or supported-environment policy, and qualify native Safari/Chrome plus repeated lifecycle/clipboard sessions. Passing isolated files is not an engine repair.

gates.summary: Qualify physical input, accessibility and touch
gates.acceptance: On the final integrated artifact, complete real IME, screen-reader, keyboard-only and supported mobile/touch testing. Earlier bounded or synthetic cases do not certify V1.

gates.summary: Approve measured latency, memory and download budgets
gates.acceptance: Set supported document/table/image/history/peer sizes and measure startup, typing, paste, Undo, reconnect and long-session memory on named hardware/browser versions. Do not silently raise existing default budgets.

Provide import/decode work isolation, TLS/identity/tenant integration, abuse limits, observability and deployment tests. Loopback demo tokens and best-effort decoder limits are not public production isolation.

gates.summary: Handle history limits, backup and compaction
gates.acceptance: Preserve Undo/Redo and outstanding offline edits across generations, as approved by the user; a history-resetting rollover does not satisfy V1. Define document lifetime at current journal/log/asset bounds, safe compaction and asset retention, coordinated restore drills and credential/writer recovery without cloning a live author.

gates.summary: Audit the actual V1 dependency and license graph
gates.acceptance: Generate and review notices/SBOM for browser, Wasm and native relay artifacts, including the pinned replication patch and decoders; verify reproducibility and vulnerability response ownership.

gates.summary: Ship coherent SDK documentation and support policy
gates.acceptance: Publish one install/quickstart, capability/support matrix, host asset/auth responsibilities, security reporting, troubleshooting, upgrade guide and contribution policy that match the actual archives.
Run sustained mixed-content use with independent collaborators, disconnects, reloads and backup restoration; record incidents, data integrity and supported operating limits.
After all required scope and qualification work, tag a reviewed RC, verify clean installs and every gate against immutable hashes, then obtain separate publication/deployment approval.
